Subject: HIPAA / BAA eligibility and PHI handling - follow up

Hi Jane —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery call and proposed next steps so we stay aligned on PHI boundaries and contract/technical items: 

Summary of what we heard
- MedWise will be sending: patient identifiers (name, DOB), lab results (structured), and physician notes (unstructured text) to Redwood for classifications and summary generation.
- Primary concern: ensure PHI is handled under a signed BAA and that data residency/segregation meets your compliance requirements.

Redwood eligibility and recommended deployment modes (high level)
- Private (VPC or on-prem): Fully eligible for BAA. Best for regulated workflows where customer controls networking and keys.
- Dedicated (reserved GPU pools): Eligible for BAA under an enterprise contract / Dedicated offering — provides tenant isolation and stronger data controls than multi-tenant hosted API.
- Hosted API (shared multitenant): Not eligible for a standard BAA. For high-compliance workloads we recommend Dedicated or Private.

PHI handling boundaries / controls we discussed
- No model training on customer data when BAA is in place; data use is restricted to inference and permitted operational needs.
- Optional retention controls: logs and request retention can be disabled or set to minimal retention windows; KV/prefix caching can be restricted per workload.
- KMS integration: Customer-managed keys (bring-your-own-key) supported in Private and available for Dedicated in enterprise contracts.

Attachments I’m sending (stubs)
- Redwood_SOC2_Summary_2026.pdf — high-level SOC 2 status and scope (Type II).
- Redwood_BAA_Template.docx — our standard BAA for review.
- MedWise_VSA_Request.xlsx — vendor security questionnaire (I started a sheet for answers we can fill in).

Proposed next steps
1) Rishi (cc) to confirm BAA coverage and any specific exclusions.
2) We’ll kick off the VSA (see attached spreadsheet) — can you confirm the procurement and security contacts we should share it with?
3) Schedule a technical call between Michael (your tech lead) and Dev (our SE) to go over network/connectivity and KMS options — I’m proposing Thursday 8/12 10:00am PT (please confirm).
4) Marissa to share SOC2 summary and BAA template (attached) + DocuSign link after you confirm procurement contact.

Thanks — I want to make this as painless as possible. If any of the above is off, please flag.

Best,
Marissa Cole

Hi Jane —

Thanks for the questions — happy to clarify. Short answers below and I’m called out where we should discuss details on the technical call.

1) Dedicated isolation and management plane
- Our Dedicated offering provides tenant isolation for inference workloads (dedicated GPU pools and resource isolation). The control/management plane (orchestration) is logically separated; for enterprise Dedicated contracts we can scope enhanced management-plane separation and contractual controls. We should capture the exact requirements and confirm during the SE call (Dev will own the technical details).

2) Hosted API and BAA
- The public Hosted API (multi-tenant) is not eligible for a standard BAA. For customers that need a BAA we require either Dedicated (enterprise contract) or Private (VPC / on-prem). There are sometimes custom arrangements for very large enterprise customers — we can discuss if MedWise expects that route.

3) PHI handling controls
- When operating under a BAA we:
  - Restrict data use to inference and permitted operational diagnostic needs only (no training).
  - Provide options to disable request retention and auditing logs beyond what’s needed for troubleshooting.
  - Support customer-managed KMS for encryption at rest and in transit.
  - Provide audit logs (for Dedicated/Private) and can integrate with your SIEM via syslog/S3 exports.

4) SOC 2 and timeline
- We maintain SOC 2 Type II (security + availability + confidentiality scope) — summary attached. For a full report we have an NDA process; procurement/security can request the full SOC 2 report and we’ll route through our security team.

I’ll be on the technical call tomorrow to confirm network/KMS details. In the meantime I’ll start the VSA responses for items that are public-facing; Marissa, can you drop the procurement contact and I’ll send the full questionnaire answers and a link to our SOC 2 distribution flow.

Thanks,
Rishi Malhotra
Head of Security, Redwood Inference
